answer.reason: The added array print guard cannot reject an array whose nesting depth was accepted by parsing. Both parsers and both print paths start at depth zero and apply the same limit to nested containers. The old harness prints only the parser-returned tree. This refutes the proposed depth-only failure for the same obligation before and after the change.

scope_contract.reason: Printing a parser-produced array belongs to the entry's parse-and-print operation.

feasible_trigger.reason: No finite input can produce a parser-accepted array at the depth rejected by the added print guard: array and object parsing reject that depth first, including mixed nesting.

observable_consequence.reason: The added guard does not cause printing to fail solely because of the depth of any parser-accepted array.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: Natural inputs already reach printing for parser-accepted arrays through the harness's buffered and ordinary print routes. The candidate's claimed blocked behavior has no reachable trigger.

identity_preserved.reason: The before and after assessment concerns the same tuple: printing an array returned by parsing at a parser-accepted nesting depth with the same old harness.
